text:
Predicates:
NiceToAnimals(x) ::: x is nice to animals.
MeanToAnimals(x) ::: x is mean to animals.
Grumpy(x) ::: x is a grumpy person.
AnimalLover(x) ::: x is an animal lover.
PetOwner(x) ::: x is a pet owner.
LovesAnimals(x) ::: x loves animals.

Premises:
∀x ¬(NiceToAnimals(x) ∧ MeanToAnimals(x)) ::: No one nice to animals is also mean to animals.
∃x (Grumpy(x) ∧ MeanToAnimals(x)) ::: Some grumpy people are mean to animals.
∀x (AnimalLover(x) → NiceToAnimals(x)) ::: All animal lovers are nice to animals.
∀x (PetOwner(x) → LovesAnimals(x)) ::: All pet owners love animals.
PetOwner(tom) ::: Tom is a pet owner.

Conclusion:
¬(Grumpy(tom) ∧ MeanToAnimals(tom)) → ¬(Grumpy(tom) ∨ AnimalLover(tom)) ::: If Tom is not both a grumpy person and mean to animals, then Tom is neither a grumpy person nor an animal lover.
